questions.question: Choose the correct definition of HTTP.

options.text: HTTP is a transport-layer protocol that establishes a reliable connection between two hosts.
HTTP is a network-layer protocol for routing packets between devices on the Internet.
HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is an application-layer protocol for transmitting hypertext (web) documents between a client and a server.
HTTP is a data storage format for exchanging structured objects between systems.

questions.correct_answer_text: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is an application-layer protocol for transmitting hypertext (web) documents between a client and a server.

questions.question: Choose the correct definition of the GET request method.

options.text: GET is an HTTP method used to submit data to be processed by a specified resource, changing server state.
GET is an HTTP method used to request data from a specified resource without modifying it.
GET is an HTTP method used to completely replace a resource with new data.
GET is an HTTP method used to remove a specified resource from the server.

questions.correct_answer_text: GET is an HTTP method used to request data from a specified resource without modifying it.

questions.question: Choose the correct definition of the POST request method.

options.text: POST is an HTTP method used to retrieve data from a resource without any side effects.
POST is an HTTP method used to replace an existing resource entirely with the provided data.
POST is an HTTP method used to delete a resource identified by a URI.
POST is an HTTP method used to send data to a server to create or process a resource, potentially changing server state.

questions.correct_answer_text: POST is an HTTP method used to send data to a server to create or process a resource, potentially changing server state.

questions.question: Choose the correct definition of the PUT method.

options.text: PUT is an HTTP method used to update or completely replace an existing resource with the data provided in the request (idempotent).
PUT is an HTTP method used only to fetch a representation of a resource.
PUT is an HTTP method used to append new data without affecting existing data, and is non-idempotent.
PUT is an HTTP method used exclusively to remove a resource from the server.

questions.correct_answer_text: PUT is an HTTP method used to update or completely replace an existing resource with the data provided in the request (idempotent).

questions.question: Choose the correct definition of the DELETE request method.

options.text: DELETE is an HTTP method used to create a new resource on the server.
DELETE is an HTTP method used to remove a specified resource from the server.
DELETE is an HTTP method used to retrieve a resource's metadata without the body.
DELETE is an HTTP method used to replace a resource's full content.

questions.correct_answer_text: DELETE is an HTTP method used to remove a specified resource from the server.

questions.question: What type of response code is 404?

options.text: A Server Error status code (5xx), indicating the server failed to fulfill a valid request.
A Redirection status code (3xx), indicating the resource has moved permanently.
A Client Error status code (4xx), meaning the requested resource was not found on the server.
A Success status code (2xx), indicating the request was accepted but no content is returned.

questions.correct_answer_text: A Client Error status code (4xx), meaning the requested resource was not found on the server.

questions.question: What is 401?

options.text: 401 Unauthorized — the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.
401 means the client is authenticated but doesn't have permission to access the resource.
401 means the requested resource could not be found on the server.
401 means the server understood the request but refuses to process it due to bad request syntax.

questions.correct_answer_text: 401 Unauthorized — the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

questions.question: Choose the correct definition of the concept 403.

options.text: 403 means the client has not provided authentication credentials at all.
403 Forbidden — the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it; the client lacks permission even with valid credentials.
403 means the requested page was permanently removed and no longer exists.
403 means the request succeeded but the server is redirecting to another resource.

questions.correct_answer_text: 403 Forbidden — the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it; the client lacks permission even with valid credentials.

questions.question: What does the number 500 mean?

options.text: 500 indicates the client sent an invalid request that the server could not understand.
500 Internal Server Error — a generic error indicating the server encountered an unexpected condition preventing it from fulfilling the request.
500 indicates the requested resource has been permanently moved to a new URL.
500 indicates the request was successful and the resource was created.

questions.correct_answer_text: 500 Internal Server Error — a generic error indicating the server encountered an unexpected condition preventing it from fulfilling the request.

questions.question: Who develops web standards?

options.text: Web standards are developed exclusively by individual browser vendors like Google and Microsoft, without any joint organization.
Web standards are developed by ICANN, the organization responsible for domain name registration.
Web standards are developed by organizations such as the W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) and WHATWG, which create and publish specifications for HTML, CSS and other web technologies.
Web standards are developed solely by IEEE, the organization responsible for electrical and electronics engineering standards.

questions.correct_answer_text: Web standards are developed by organizations such as the W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) and WHATWG, which create and publish specifications for HTML, CSS and other web technologies.

questions.question: What is an IP address?

options.text: An IP address is a human-readable domain name used to identify a website.
An IP address is a unique numerical label assigned to each device connected to a network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication, identifying the host and its location on the network.
An IP address is a unique hardware identifier burned into a network card by its manufacturer.
An IP address is a port number used to identify a specific application running on a device.

questions.correct_answer_text: An IP address is a unique numerical label assigned to each device connected to a network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication, identifying the host and its location on the network.

questions.question: What is a subnet mask?

options.text: A subnet mask is the address used to identify the default gateway of a network.
A subnet mask is a 32-bit number that divides an IP address into network and host portions, determining which part identifies the network and which identifies the device.
A subnet mask is a unique identifier assigned to a device's network interface by the manufacturer.
A subnet mask is a table that maps domain names to IP addresses.

questions.correct_answer_text: A subnet mask is a 32-bit number that divides an IP address into network and host portions, determining which part identifies the network and which identifies the device.

questions.question: What is TCP/IP?

options.text: TCP/IP is a single protocol responsible only for translating domain names into IP addresses.
TCP/IP is a markup language used to structure content on web pages.
TCP/IP is a suite of communication protocols used to interconnect network devices on the Internet, defining how data is packetized, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received.
TCP/IP is a security protocol used exclusively for encrypting data transmitted over HTTPS.

questions.correct_answer_text: TCP/IP is a suite of communication protocols used to interconnect network devices on the Internet, defining how data is packetized, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received.

questions.question: Which JS statement guarantees that a code block executes at least once, even if the condition is false?

options.text: while
if...else
for
do...while

questions.correct_answer_text: do...while

questions.question: Which JS statement represents branching?

options.text: for
if...else
while
do...while

questions.correct_answer_text: if...else

questions.question: What will the following code fragment return: var result = !("false" == false)?

options.text: false
undefined
true
NaN

questions.correct_answer_text: true

questions.question: What happens when the following code fragment, using the symbol data type in JS, is executed?

options.text: result will be true, because symbols with identical descriptions are considered equal.
The code throws a TypeError, because symbols cannot be compared using the strict equality operator.
result will be false, because symbols are always unique, even with an identical description.
result will be true, because JavaScript caches symbols with the same description like it does with string primitives.

questions.correct_answer_text: result will be false, because symbols are always unique, even with an identical description.

questions.question: What is the difference between "weak" references and "strong" references?

options.text: A "weak" reference can only point to primitive values, while a "strong" reference can only point to objects.

A strong reference keeps its target object alive in memory as long as the reference exists, preventing garbage collection; a weak reference does not prevent the referenced object from being garbage collected.
A strong reference is created only inside functions, while a weak reference is created only in the global scope.
A weak reference always executes asynchronously, while a strong reference always executes synchronously.

questions.correct_answer_text: A strong reference keeps its target object alive in memory as long as the reference exists, preventing garbage collection; a weak reference does not prevent the referenced object from being garbage collected.

questions.question: What is stored in the Call Stack?

options.text: Objects that are waiting to be garbage collected.
Information about the active function calls of a program — which function is currently executing and which functions were called to get there, in LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) order.
Callback functions waiting to be executed after asynchronous operations complete.
Variable declarations for the entire duration of the program, regardless of function execution.

questions.correct_answer_text: Information about the active function calls of a program — which function is currently executing and which functions were called to get there, in LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) order.
